newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday March 3.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime Minister Romano Prodi praised opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi on Sunday for expressing willingness to back a mini-budget providing the measures to help Italy join the European single currency. In a statement, Prodi said "the willingness shown by the leader of Freedom Alliance Silvio Berlusconi to vote for the government's public finance provisions is an act of responsibility that does him honour" (all).

* Both far-right national Alliance leader Gianfranco Fini, Berlusconi's main coalition partner, and hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti, on whose support the government relies for a majority in the lower house of parliament, criticised the "opening" of this Prodi-Berlusconi dialogue. Bertinotti warned Prodi against what he called Berlusconi's "poisoned chalice" (all).

* Centre right Freedom Alliance named Gabriele Albertini, chairman of metalworkers employers association Federmeccanica, as its candidate for Milan's mayor election due in April. Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi might lead the Freedom Alliance list of candidates for which would determine the party's representation within the city government (all).

* Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said Italy was seeking a European meeting on Albania, where a state of emergency has been declared, while prime minister Romano Prodi phoned to president Sali Berisha (all).

* Tresury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi replies to Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti saying that the labour agreement of July 1993 is still valid. Romiti has called for more flexible labour laws to help revive Italy's poor south, adding that the accord on the cost of labour is due for revision (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
